claim: β-Lactam antibiotics are the most important and widely used antibacterial agents across the world.
source: β-Lactam antibiotics are the most important and widely used antibacterial agents across the world.
evidence: This is a general statement about β-lactam antibiotics that is commonly accepted in the field.

claim: The widespread dissemination of β-lactamases among pathogenic bacteria limits the efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics.
source: However, the widespread dissemination of β-lactamases among pathogenic bacteria limits the efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about antibiotic resistance mechanisms.

claim: Effective clinically approved inhibitors against class B metallo-β-lactamases are not available.
source: yet, effective clinically approved inhibitors against class B metallo-β-lactamases are not available.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of clinical therapeutics.

claim: L1 is a class B3 enzyme expressed by Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.
source: L1, a class B3 enzyme expressed by Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, is a significant contributor to the β-lactam resistance displayed by this opportunistic pathogen.
evidence: This is a classification statement supported by established literature.

claim: L1 is a tetramer with two elongated loops (α3-β7 and β12-α5) present around the active site of each monomer.
source: Structurally, L1 is a tetramer with two elongated loops, α3-β7 and β12-α5, present around the active site of each monomer.
evidence: This structural description is supported by crystallographic data.

claim: Residues in the α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops influence substrate/inhibitor binding.
source: Residues in these two loops influence substrate/inhibitor binding.
evidence: This is inferred from structural and functional studies.

claim: Enhanced sampling molecular dynamics simulations were performed to study conformational changes of the elongated loops.
source: To study how the conformational changes of the elongated loops affect the active site in each monomer, enhanced sampling molecular dynamics simulations were performed, Markov State Models were built, and convolutional variational autoencoder-based deep learning was applied.
evidence: This describes the computational methodology used in the study.

claim: Key residues D150a, H151, P225, Y227, and R236 were mutated and the activity of the generated L1 variants was evaluated in cell-based experiments.
source: The key identified residues (D150a, H151, P225, Y227, and R236) were mutated and the activity of the generated L1 variants was evaluated in cell-based experiments.
evidence: This describes the experimental validation performed in the study.

claim: There are extremely significant gating interactions between α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops.
source: The results demonstrate that there are extremely significant gating interactions between α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the computational and experimental results.

claim: The gating interactions with the conformational changes of the key residues play an important role in the structural remodeling of the active site.
source: Taken together, the gating interactions with the conformational changes of the key residues play an important role in the structural remodeling of the active site.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: β-lactam antibiotics accounted for 65% of all antibiotics prescriptions in the United States.
source: Penicillins, carbapenems, cephalosporins, and monobactams are typical β-lactam antibiotics on the market and, accounted for 65% of all antibiotics prescriptions in the United States (Bush and Bradford, 2016).
evidence: This statistic is cited from Bush and Bradford, 2016.

claim: The β-lactam ring acts as a false substrate for transpeptidases and inhibits peptidoglycan cross-linking.
source: A common structural feature in this exceptionally large class of antibiotics is the presence of a β-lactam ring, which acts as a false substrate for the transpeptidases (also called Penicillin-binding proteins, PBPs) and inhibits peptidoglycan cross-linking, thereby impairing the synthesis of the bacterial cell wall (Palzkill, 2018).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of action of β-lactam antibiotics, supported by citation.

claim: The World Health Organization projected in 2019 that drug resistance could cause up to 10 million deaths annually by 2050.
source: The World Health Organization projected in 2019 that such drug resistance could cause up to 10 million deaths annually by 2050 ('No time to Wait', n.d.).
evidence: This is a projection cited from a WHO report.

claim: The expression of β-lactamases is the most common mechanism found in various bacteria resistant to β-lactams.
source: Among these, the expression of β-lactamases is the most common mechanism found in various bacteria resistant to β-lactams (Lingzhi et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Lingzhi et al., 2018.

claim: β-Lactamases inactivate β-lactam antibiotics by hydrolyzing the amide bond in the β-lactam ring.
source: β-Lactamases inactivate β-lactam antibiotics by hydrolyzing the amide bond in the β-lactam ring.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of β-lactamase action.

claim: Classes A, C, and D are serine β-lactamases, while class B groups the zinc-dependent metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs).
source: While classes A, C, and D are serine β-lactamases, class B groups the zinc-dependent metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs).
evidence: This is a classification of β-lactamases based on established nomenclature.

claim: MBLs employ one or two zinc ions at the active site as catalytic cofactors.
source: MBLs employ one or two zinc ions at the active site as catalytic cofactors (Palzkill, 2013; Tooke et al., 2019).
evidence: This structural feature is cited from literature.

claim: MBLs are subdivided into three subclasses (B1, B2, and B3) based on their sequence, metal content, and different active site features.
source: MBLs are further subdivided into three subclasses (B1, B2, and B3) based on their sequence, metal content, and different active site features (Bahr et al., 2022; Bahr et al., 2021).
evidence: This classification is supported by citations.

claim: All MBLs adopt the αβ/βα sandwich motif.
source: All MBLs adopt the αβ/βα sandwich motif and have mono- (class B2) or binucleated zinc (classes B1 and B3) at the active site.
evidence: This is a structural characteristic of MBLs.

claim: B1 and B3 subclasses have a broad-spectrum substrate profile that includes penicillins, cephalosporins, and carbapenems.
source: The B1 and B3 subclasses have a broad-spectrum substrate profile that includes penicillins, cephalosporins, and carbapenems, while the B2 enzymes exhibit a narrow profile that includes carbapenems (Palzkill, 2013; Tooke et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the substrate specificity of MBL subclasses, supported by citations.

claim: B2 enzymes exhibit a narrow profile that includes carbapenems.
source: The B1 and B3 subclasses have a broad-spectrum substrate profile that includes penicillins, cephalosporins, and carbapenems, while the B2 enzymes exhibit a narrow profile that includes carbapenems (Palzkill, 2013; Tooke et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the substrate specificity of B2 MBLs, supported by citations.

claim: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is a non-fermenting, Gram-negative bacillus that has emerged as an opportunistic pathogen.
source: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is a non-fermenting, Gram-negative bacillus that has emerged as an opportunistic pathogen.
evidence: This is a microbiological description of the organism.

claim: S. maltophilia mainly affects patients with cancer, cystic fibrosis, and other conditions leading to an immunosuppressed state.
source: This organism mainly affects patients with cancer, cystic fibrosis, and other conditions leading to an immunosuppressed state, where it can cause a variety of clinical syndromes, mainly pulmonary and blood stream infections (Mojica et al., 2019).
evidence: This clinical information is supported by citation.

claim: Crude mortality rates range from 14% to 69% in patients with bloodstream infection due to S. maltophilia.
source: Crude mortality rates range from 14% to 69% in patients with bloodstream infection due to S. maltophilia (Adegoke et al., 2017; Brooke et al., 2017; Crisp et al., 2007).
evidence: This mortality statistic is supported by multiple citations.

claim: β-Lactams resistance in S. maltophilia is mediated by the coordinated expression of L1 metallo-β-lactamase together with L2 β-lactamase.
source: β-Lactams resistance in S. maltophilia is mediated by the coordinated expression of L1 metallo-β-lactamase (class B3 MBL) together with L2 β-lactamase (class A β-lactamase) (Okazaki and Avison, 2008).
evidence: This mechanism of resistance is cited from Okazaki and Avison, 2008.

claim: L1 MBL can hydrolyze almost all β-lactam antibiotics with the exception of monobactams such as aztreonam.
source: L1 MBL can hydrolyze almost all β-lactam antibiotics with the exception of monobactams such as aztreonam and is resistant to all clinically available β-lactamase inhibitors (Brooke, 2012; Mojica et al., 2019; Okazaki and Avison, 2008).
evidence: This describes the substrate profile of L1 MBL, supported by citations.

claim: L1 MBL is resistant to all clinically available β-lactamase inhibitors.
source: L1 MBL can hydrolyze almost all β-lactam antibiotics with the exception of monobactams such as aztreonam and is resistant to all clinically available β-lactamase inhibitors (Brooke, 2012; Mojica et al., 2019; Okazaki and Avison, 2008).
evidence: This statement about inhibitor resistance is supported by citations.

claim: L1 MBL is the only known β-lactamase that functions as a tetramer.
source: L1 MBL is unique among all known β-lactamases as it is the only known β-lactamase that functions as a tetramer (Figure 1A).
evidence: This structural uniqueness is stated and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: In each subunit of L1 MBL, there are two zinc ions bound at the active site.
source: In each subunit, there are two zinc ions bound at the active site (Figure 1B, Ullah et al., 1998).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B and cited from Ullah et al., 1998.

claim: The first Zinc (Zn1) is in a tetrahedral coordination with a water molecule and three histidine residues.
source: The first Zinc (Zn1) is in a tetrahedral coordination with a water molecule and three histidine residues.
evidence: This describes the coordination geometry of Zn1.

claim: The second Zinc (Zn2) is coordinated by two histidine, one aspartic acid and a water molecule in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry.
source: The second Zinc (Zn2) is coordinated by two histidine, one aspartic acid and a water molecule in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry.
evidence: This describes the coordination geometry of Zn2.

claim: A water molecule that acts like a nucleophile for the catalytic reaction bridges the two zinc ions.
source: Another water molecule, which acts like a nucleophile for the catalytic reaction bridges the two zinc ions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the catalytic mechanism, illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both zinc ions are relevant for hydrolysis and protein folding in L1.
source: Studies have revealed that both zinc ions are relevant for hydrolysis and protein folding in L1 (Crisp et al., 2007; Hu et al., 2008; Ullah et al., 1998).
evidence: This functional role is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The L1 MBL tetramer is held tightly by three discrete sets of hydrophobic interactions.
source: The L1 MBL tetramer is held tightly by three discrete sets of hydrophobic interactions, which allows each monomer to make contacts with the other three subunits (Crisp et al., 2007; Sevaille et al., 2017; Ullah et al., 1998).
evidence: This structural feature is supported by citations.

claim: Each monomer buries 1300 Å2 of non-polar side-chain surface area on the formation of the tetramer.
source: All these interactions are primarily hydrophobic and lead to each monomer burying 1300 Å2 of non-polar side-chain surface area on the formation of the tetramer.
evidence: This quantifies the buried surface area in tetramer formation.

claim: The side chain of M175 penetrates a shallow pocket formed by E141, L150d, P198, and Y236 on the surface of the adjacent subunit.
source: The key interactions made by the side chain of M175 penetrating a shallow pocket formed by E141, L150d, P198, and Y236 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2; after the standard BBL numbering Garau et al., 2004) on the surface of the adjacent subunit, has been shown to be essential for stabilizing the tetramer (Simm et al., 2002).
evidence: This interaction is described and referenced to Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and cited from Simm et al., 2002.

claim: A substitution of M175 results in failure of tetramerization and a reduced activity against most β-lactams of ca. two orders of magnitude.
source: A substitution of this M175 results in failure of tetramerization and a reduced activity against most β-lactams of ca. two orders of magnitude (Simm et al., 2002).
evidence: This experimental result is cited from Simm et al., 2002.

claim: The α3-β7 loop at the N-terminal extension has 20 residues (G149-D171) and extends over the active site.
source: The α3-β7 loop at the N-terminal extension has 20 residues (G149-D171) and extends over the active site (Garrity et al., 2004).
evidence: This structural description is cited from Garrity et al., 2004.

claim: Residues in the α3-β7 loop are considered to be involved in determining the spectrum of the enzyme by forming hydrophobic interactions with large hydrophobic motifs at C2 or C6 of β-lactam substrates.
source: These residues are considered to be involved in determining the spectrum of the enzyme by forming hydrophobic interactions with large hydrophobic motifs at C2 or C6 of β-lactam substrates (Sevaille et al., 2017; Spencer et al., 2005; Spencer et al., 2001; Ullah et al., 1998).
evidence: This functional role is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The G159A substitution disrupts the positioning of F156 by decreasing the flexibility of the loop.
source: This substitution disrupts the positioning of F156, another significant residue involved in the function of L1, by decreasing the flexibility of the loop.
evidence: This describes the effect of the G159A mutation.

claim: The G161D substitution can affect the efficiency of the enzyme catalytic activity.
source: Similarly, the G161D substitution can also affect the efficiency of the enzyme catalytic activity (Carenbauer et al., 2002; Nauton et al., 2008; Spencer et al., 2005; Ullah et al., 1998).
evidence: This effect is supported by citations.

claim: The β12-α5 loop consists of 19 residues (A219-H239) and lies adjacent to the active site.
source: The β12-α5 loop consists of 19 residues (A219-H239) and lies adjacent to the active site.
evidence: This is a structural description of the β12-α5 loop.

claim: S221 in the β12-α5 loop makes indirect interaction with Zn2.
source: S221 in this loop makes indirect interaction with Zn2, while S223 serves as a second-shell residue of H196 (Crisp et al., 2007; Mojica et al., 2019; Ullah et al., 1998).
evidence: This interaction is supported by citations.

claim: S223 serves as a second-shell residue of H196.
source: S221 in this loop makes indirect interaction with Zn2, while S223 serves as a second-shell residue of H196 (Crisp et al., 2007; Mojica et al., 2019; Ullah et al., 1998).
evidence: This structural relationship is supported by citations.

claim: S221 coordinates a Zn2-bound apical water.
source: S221 coordinates a Zn2-bound apical water, whereas S223 directly interacts with the substrate C4 carboxylate group (Spencer et al., 2005).
evidence: This interaction is cited from Spencer et al., 2005.

claim: S223 directly interacts with the substrate C4 carboxylate group.
source: S221 coordinates a Zn2-bound apical water, whereas S223 directly interacts with the substrate C4 carboxylate group (Spencer et al., 2005).
evidence: This interaction is cited from Spencer et al., 2005.

claim: In a recent crystal structure, S221 and S223 have been found to directly interact with substrates.
source: In a recent crystal structure, S221 and S223 have been found to directly interact with substrates (Twidale et al., 2021).
evidence: This observation is cited from Twidale et al., 2021.

claim: Novel substitutions Q230R, (K/Q)232R, G233D, and (P/A)235V have been identified in the β12-α5 loop.
source: Besides, novel substitutions have been identified in the loop, namely Q230R, (K/Q)232R, G233D, and (P/A)235V (Mojica et al., 2019).
evidence: These substitutions are cited from Mojica et al., 2019.

claim: The apical points of α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops are positioned at the interface between monomers.
source: The apical points of α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops are positioned at the interface between monomers, and direct interaction with residues that affects the catalytic activity of the L1 MBL has been confirmed (Ullah et al., 1998).
evidence: This structural observation is cited from Ullah et al., 1998.

claim: The crystal structure of L1 MBL has been determined in apo state and in complex with inhibitors and final reaction products.
source: The crystal structure of L1 MBL has been determined in apo state and in complex with inhibitors and final reaction products (Nauton et al., 2008; Sevaille et al., 2017; Twidale et al., 2021; Ullah et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by multiple crystallographic studies.

claim: In the apo state, the β12-α5 loop is collapsed on the active site.
source: In the apo state, the β12-α5 loop is collapsed on the active site.
evidence: This describes the conformation observed in crystal structures.

claim: In complex structures, the β12-α5 loop wraps around to enclose the substrate/inhibitor within the active site.
source: In complex structures, the β12-α5 loop wraps around to enclose the substrate/inhibitor within the active site.
evidence: This describes the conformation observed in complex crystal structures.

claim: The conformation of the α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops are identical in all structures, be it in the apo state or in complex with substrate/inhibitors.
source: It is worth noting that the conformation of the α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops are identical in all structures, be it in the apo state or in complex with substrate/inhibitors.
evidence: This observation is based on comparison of crystal structures.

claim: In the collapsed, closed conformation, residues R236 (β12-α5) and D150c (α3-β7) form a salt bridge interaction.
source: In this collapsed, closed conformation, residues R236 (β12-α5) and D150c (α3-β7) form a salt bridge interaction; Y227 (β12-α5) forms a π–π stacking interaction with H151 (α3-β7) and P225 (β12-α5) adopts an 'in' conformation, where the Cγ atom in the cyclic side chain of P225 is 6.5 Å from the centroid of the two Zinc ions (Figure 1B).
evidence: This interaction is described and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Y227 (β12-α5) forms a π–π stacking interaction with H151 (α3-β7).
source: In this collapsed, closed conformation, residues R236 (β12-α5) and D150c (α3-β7) form a salt bridge interaction; Y227 (β12-α5) forms a π–π stacking interaction with H151 (α3-β7) and P225 (β12-α5) adopts an 'in' conformation, where the Cγ atom in the cyclic side chain of P225 is 6.5 Å from the centroid of the two Zinc ions (Figure 1B).
evidence: This interaction is described and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: P225 (β12-α5) adopts an 'in' conformation, where the Cγ atom in the cyclic side chain of P225 is 6.5 Å from the centroid of the two Zinc ions.
source: In this collapsed, closed conformation, residues R236 (β12-α5) and D150c (α3-β7) form a salt bridge interaction; Y227 (β12-α5) forms a π–π stacking interaction with H151 (α3-β7) and P225 (β12-α5) adopts an 'in' conformation, where the Cγ atom in the cyclic side chain of P225 is 6.5 Å from the centroid of the two Zinc ions (Figure 1B).
evidence: This conformation is described and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: An additional interaction between the side chain of Q310 (α6 helix) and the backbone carbonyl oxygen of A224 (β12-α5) stabilizes the loops in the closed conformation.
source: An additional interaction between the side chain of the Q310 (α6 helix) and the backbone carbonyl oxygen of A224 (β12-α5) stabilizes the loops in the closed conformation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This stabilizing interaction is described and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Inter-subunit interactions are the major contributors that affect the flexibility of α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops.
source: Previous studies have shown that the inter-subunit interactions are the major contributors that affect the flexibility of α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops, and the dynamics of these loops can directly influence β-lactam binding and catalysis (Spencer et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from Spencer et al., 2005.

claim: The dynamics of α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops can directly influence β-lactam binding and catalysis.
source: Previous studies have shown that the inter-subunit interactions are the major contributors that affect the flexibility of α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops, and the dynamics of these loops can directly influence β-lactam binding and catalysis (Spencer et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from Spencer et al., 2005.

claim: A converged MSM with seven metastable states was successfully built using the backbone torsions and the Cα-RMSD of the α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops, at a lag time of 5 ns.
source: A converged MSM with seven metastable states was successfully built using the backbone torsions and the Cα-RMSD of the α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops, at a lag time of 5 ns (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the MSM construction, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The dynamics of the two loops (α3-β7 and β12-α5) can be described by closed, intermediate, and open conformations.
source: The dynamics of the two loops (α3-β7 and β12-α5) can be described by closed, intermediate, and open conformations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This classification is based on the simulation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 'closed' conformations of the loop is defined by the collective formation of a salt bridge between D150c-R236 (α3-β7 and β12-α5), H151-Y227 π–π stacking interaction and P225 adopting an 'in' conformation.
source: The 'closed' conformations of the loop is defined by the collective formation of a salt bridge between D150c-R236 (α3-β7 and β12-α5), H151-Y227 π–π stacking interaction and P225 adopting an 'in' conformation (Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplements 2–4).
evidence: This definition is based on simulation data shown in multiple figures.

claim: The loops are collapsed on the active site resulting in an occluded 420.4 ± 94.8 Å3 cavity in the closed state.
source: The loops are collapsed on the active site resulting in an occluded 420.4 ± 94.8 Å3 cavity (Figure 3A).
evidence: This volume calculation is from simulation data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: State 7 defines the closed conformation of L1 MBL, with the Cα-RMSD comparison with the apo state crystal structure (PDB id 1SML) to be 0.79 Å and with inhibitor complex (PDB id 5DPX) is 0.77 Å.
source: State 7 defines the closed conformation of L1 MBL, with the Cα-RMSD comparison with the apo state crystal structure (PDB id 1SML) to be 0.79 Å and with inhibitor complex (PDB id 5DPX) is 0.77 Å (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This RMSD comparison is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: State 7 is the most populated, with 80% of all conformations falling within this cluster.
source: State 7 is the most populated, with 80% of all conformations falling within this cluster.
evidence: This population statistic is from the MSM analysis.

claim: State 7 is the lowest energy state.
source: State 7 is also the lowest energy state.
evidence: This is determined from the MSM free energy calculations.

claim: The closed state dominates the dynamics.
source: These observations allow us to conclude that the closed state dominates the dynamics and also explains why this conformation is always resolved in crystallographic experiments.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the MSM population analysis.

claim: State 4 is an intermediate open conformation where two or more interactions including the D150c-R236 salt bridge, H151-Y227 π–π stacking, are lost and P225 adopts the 'out' conformation.
source: State 4 is an intermediate open conformation (Figure 3B), where two or more interactions including the D150c-R236 salt bridge, H151-Y227 π–π stacking, are lost and P225 adopts the 'out' conformation.
evidence: This describes state 4 based on simulation data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The average volume calculated in the intermediate state is 608.3 ± 137.25 Å3.
source: The average volume calculated in the intermediate state is 608.3 ± 137.25 Å3.
evidence: This volume calculation is from simulation data.

claim: In the open conformation (state 1), the D150c-R236 salt bridge interaction is broken, the H151-Y227 π–π stacking interaction is lost and the cyclic side chain of P225 orients away from the active site and adopts an 'out' conformation.
source: In the open conformation (state 1), the D150c-R236 salt bridge interaction is broken, the H151-Y227 π–π stacking interaction is lost and the cyclic side chain of P225 orients away from the active site and adopts an 'out' conformation.
evidence: This describes state 1 based on simulation data.

claim: The loss of constraints around the loop allows the side chain of Y227 to rotate, with the hydroxyl group orienting toward R236 and away from the active site in the open state.
source: The loss of constraints around the loop allows the side chain of Y227 to rotate, with the hydroxyl group orienting toward R236 and away from the active site.
evidence: This conformational change is observed in simulation data.

claim: The total volume of the merged cavity in the open state is 1027.17 ± 191.04 Å3.
source: The total volume of the merged cavity is 1027.17 ± 191.04 Å3 and is large enough for the substrates to access the zinc metal center.
evidence: This volume calculation is from simulation data.

claim: The shortest mean first passage time in the flux pathways is between states 1 → 4 → 7.
source: The shortest mean first passage time in the flux pathways is between states 1 → 4 → 7, which indicates that the free energy (FE) barrier along this path is low (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is calculated from the MSM and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The flux pathway 1 → 4 → 7 shows predominant prevalence (89.7%) at equilibrium.
source: This can explain why this flux pathway shows predominant prevalence (89.7%) at equilibrium.
evidence: This percentage is calculated from the MSM analysis.

claim: An unsupervised CVAE-based deep learning was performed to identify dynamic changes in the α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops.
source: To resolve this, an unsupervised CVAE-based deep learning was performed (Bhowmik et al., 2018; Romero et al., 2019). The CVAE provides biophysically relevant information related to conformational transitions induced by changes in interactions. More specifically, CVAE was used to identify dynamic changes in the α3-β7 and β12-α5 loops resulting from changes in D150c-R236 salt bridge, H151-Y227 π–π stacking interaction and the 'in/out' conformation of P225.
evidence: This describes the deep learning methodology applied, with citations.

claim: The deep learning is able to cluster individual subunits in the tetramer based on their local and global conformational dynamics.
source: The combined deep learning is able to cluster individual subunits in the tetramer based on their local and global conformational dynamics (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This result is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Subunits A and C share similar dynamics, while subunits B and D are clustered in the same tSNE space.
source: Subunits A and C share similar dynamics, while subunits B and D are clustered in the same tSNE space (Figure 4A).
evidence: This clustering result is shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The most flexible subunit is D, where all three, 'open–intermediate–closed' states are observed.
source: The most flexible subunit is D, where all three, 'open–intermediate–closed' states are observed.
evidence: This is observed from the CVAE analysis.

claim: The salt bridge formation between D150c-R236 (α3-β7 and β12-α5) is crucial for the function of L1 MBL.
source: The salt bridge formation between D150c-R236 (α3-β7 and β12-α5) is crucial for the function of L1 MBL (Simm et al., 2002).
evidence: This importance is cited from Simm et al., 2002.

claim: The salt bridge acts as a gate, and the formation/loss of the salt bridge regulates the highly mobile β12-α5 loop to adopt an open/closed conformation.
source: This salt bridge acts as a gate, and the formation/loss of the salt bridge regulates the highly mobile β12-α5 loop to adopt an open/closed conformation.
evidence: This gating mechanism is inferred from the simulation data.

claim: Disruption of the salt bridge between R164 and D179 in TEM-1 would alter the structure of the substrate-binding site by restructuring the conformation of the Ω-loop, decreasing the antibiotic resistance.
source: Previous experiments on TEM-1, a class A β-lactamase, offered evidence for the significance of salt bridge formation between important loops (Vakulenko et al., 1995). Disruption of the salt bridge between R164 and D179 would in turn alter the structure of the substrate-binding site by restructuring the conformation of the Ω-loop, decreasing the antibiotic resistance (Vakulenko et al., 1995).
evidence: This is cited from experimental work on TEM-1 by Vakulenko et al., 1995.

claim: The π–π stacking interaction between H151 and Y227 is another important interaction that stabilizes the loops.
source: The π–π stacking interaction between H151 and Y227 is another important interaction that stabilizes the loops.
evidence: This is inferred from the simulation data.

claim: π–π stacking interaction is considered a very important interaction in protein folding and molecular recognition.
source: Such π–π stacking interaction is considered a very important interaction in protein folding and molecular recognition (Brylinski, 2018).
evidence: This is cited from Brylinski, 2018.

claim: Studies on other β-lactamases have revealed that the π–π stacking near the substrate-binding site can help stabilize the binding site topology and contribute to the recognition of the antibiotics.
source: Studies on other β-lactamases have revealed that the π–π stacking near the substrate-binding site can help stabilize the binding site topology and contribute to the recognition of the antibiotics (Hargis et al., 2014; Langan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from studies on other β-lactamases.

claim: The side chain of P225 exists in trans configuration in L1 MBL, which is very unusual among the β-lactamases.
source: The side chain of P225 exists in trans configuration in L1 MBL, which is very unusual among the β-lactamases.
evidence: This is an observation from structural analysis.

claim: Usually, in β-lactamases, the proline is found in the cis configuration.
source: Usually, in β-lactamases, the proline is found in the cis configuration.
evidence: This is general knowledge about β-lactamases.

claim: Studies on TEM-1 β-lactamase have revealed the importance of the proline cis configuration in the protein folding and correct orientation of residues involved in the catalytic reaction.
source: Studies on TEM-1 β-lactamase have already revealed the importance of the proline cis configuration in the protein folding and correct orientation of residues involved in the catalytic reaction (Vanhove et al., 1996; Vanhove et al., 1995).
evidence: This is cited from studies on TEM-1.

claim: The ω torsion angle of P225 is stable at ca. −180° in all four monomers, while also often transitioning to ca. 180°, confirming the trans configuration of P225.
